subject: Proposal: rebalance p50/p95 measurement windows + transient-noise carveout
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@opsly.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Clarify hosted API p50/p95 windows — noisy bursts in US-East

Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team is impressed with the throughput. One thing came up in our SRE review: our traffic pattern on US-East has significant short bursts tied to batch jobs (1–3 min) and we want to avoid those inflating p95 measurements for SLA triggers.

Can Redwood propose concrete measurement windows and any transient-noise carveouts you support for Hosted API p50/p95 commitments? We need this detail for our procurement and to include in the RFP.

High-level asks:
- p50 and p95 targets you can commit to for regular user-facing traffic (not batch heavy jobs)
- measurement window (sliding 5m/1h/daily?) and aggregation method (rolling percentile vs per-minute buckets)
- any transient carveouts (regional bursts, known maintenance, short-lived autoscaling events) and how they’re defined

Copied procurement for visibility.

—Sara
Sara Patel
Head of SRE, Opsly Inc.

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Sara Patel <sara@opsly.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 13:48:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify hosted API p50/p95 windows — noisy bursts in US-East

Sara — thanks for the clear summary and for surfacing the procurement requirements. I pulled our hosted SLO playbook together into a short proposal (high level below) and attached a first-pass SLA addendum you can share with procurement.

Proposal (summary):
- Commitments: p50 = 65 ms, p95 = 210 ms for user-facing requests routed to "hosted-us-east" cluster under normal operating conditions. These numbers reflect our optimised kernels + prefix caching profile for conversational workloads.
- Measurement windows: primary measurement is a rolling 1-hour window computed from per-second samples and aggregated with a rolling quantile algorithm (we report p50/p95 over the rolling 1-hour). We also retain a 24-hour aggregated view for trend/backfill.
- Transient-noise carveout: we propose a transparent carveout for short bursts defined as any contiguous spike period where 95th-percentile(1m) > 2x historical 95th-percentile(1m) AND duration < 10 minutes. These flagged intervals are excluded from SLA breach calculations after automated verification against autoscaling activity and capacity events. This is conservative and intended to catch short noisy migrations or customer-side batch floods.
- Canary & rollforward: changes to kernel/quantization that may shift latency are deployed behind a canary; until canary stabilises for 48 hours we exclude canary traffic from SLA windows for that model variant.

Attachments: opsly_sla_addendum_draft_v1.pdf (contains redlineable language for procurement).

Open items I’d like your feedback on:
1) Does your team want the carveout duration tightened (we default to 10m) or expanded?
2) Do you require a regional carveout (US-East only) or global carveout policy?
3) Any procurement milestones that require more prescriptive SLAs (e.g., calendarized maintenance windows)?

If that plan looks okay I can loop in legal to prepare an SLA addendum and we’ll include a HubSpot milestone for procurement.

—Markus Klein
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, Sara Patel <sara@opsly.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify hosted API p50/p95 windows — noisy bursts in US-East

Adding a few practical options from the ops side so procurement has clearer choices. I’m recommending the following concrete measurement/alerting approach we can include in the SLA addendum: 

Option A (strict):
- p50 65 ms / p95 210 ms measured on rolling 1-hour quantile
- Exclude only scheduled maintenance and confirmed infra incidents
- Automatic monitoring alerts if 5 consecutive 1m buckets exceed p95 by >25%

Option B (balanced — recommended for Opsly):
- Same p50/p95 numbers but use the transient-noise carveout as Markus outlined: 1m bucket threshold >2x baseline and duration <10m
- We will auto-flag candidate carveouts and provide a 48-hour review window; flagged intervals are transparently listed in the monthly SLA report.

Option C (lenient):
- p95 measured on rolling 3-hour window with carveouts allowed up to 30 minutes for short-lived burst traffic (useful if you expect job-triggered bursts)

Operational notes:
- We publish per-route token-level latency histograms to a shared dashboard (read-only link) so your SREs can verify flagged intervals before procurement accepts the carveout language.
- For billing-sensitive incidents, we’ll provide exported latency aggregates and traces (PII-redacted) per HubSpot request under NDA.

If Opsly wants Option B we’ll bake that into opsly_sla_addendum_draft_v1.pdf and prepare a concise 1-page summary for procurement.

—Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Patel <sara@opsly.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@opsly.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 15:06:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify hosted API p50/p95 windows — noisy bursts in US-East

Thanks Markus and Ben — this is very helpful. Opsly prefers Option B (balanced) with the 10-minute carveout. Two small asks before procurement signs: 

1) Can Redwood include an explicit clause that carveout flags will be accompanied by the raw 1m-bucket histogram for the flagged interval within 48 hours? That will speed our internal verification.
2) Timeline: procurement needs a redlineable SLA addendum by EOD next Wednesday so we can get legal review and an internal approval meeting the following week.

I’ve attached our procurement spreadsheet with target dates and internal approvers: procurement_requirements.xlsx.

If you send the redline today/tomorrow we’ll prioritize review.

—Sara
Head of SRE, Opsly Inc.
